title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Context. This is Grothendieck's 1986 'Analysis situs (deuxième mouture)', an axiomatic, point-free style theory of 'figures' in a tame-topology setting. Figures have 'shadows' Om/Omb(F), which behave like subsets of an underlying space. Relations used on this page:
- F' ≪ F: F' lies inside the interior of F. Compare 'x ∈ Om(X)° i.e. x ≪ X'.
- G ∥ F: G and F are dissociated, i.e. their shadows are disjoint.
- G ∦ F (written with an overbar): G and F meet.
- M, L: distinguished classes of elementary figures (pieces), with L apparently the smallest ones ('points' or small cells).
The atlas axioms At 9, At 9_Σ, At 10, At 11 bis, At 12 were streamlined on the previous page.

What the page does. Grothendieck announces that he now turns to subdivisions, 'which had not yet come up at all!'. He first wanted to state the following as an axiom, then crossed out 'Axiome' and wrote 'Proposition':
- Statement. Let F be a figure and F' ≪ F. Suppose some non-empty figure G satisfies G ∥ F' and G ∦ F. Then such a G can be chosen with G ≪ F.
- Topological meaning. If the shadow of F is not covered by the shadow of F', then some non-empty piece lying in the interior of F avoids F'. This is a regularity property: closed figures should be the closure of their interior, or more precisely 'F minus F' meets int F'.

Proof sketch begun on this page.
1. One may replace G by an elementary piece X ∈ M, and then by an x ∈ L inside Omb(G). He cross-refers to (1.58), p. 59.
2. He looks for a minimal statement implying the proposition. The hypothesis G ∦ F gives, via At 9, a point y ∈ Om G and x ∈ Om F with x ∦ y. Moreover y ∥ F', since G ∥ F'.
3. Choose X ∈ F with x ∈ Om(X)°, i.e. x ≪ X. This gives the diagram F' ≪ F ⊇ F'_X ≪ X ⊇ x, with y alongside. Here F'_X is the restriction of F' to X.

Continuation on p. 82. The goal is to find z ∈ omb(X)° with z ∥ F'_X. Then z ≪ X ≤ F, so z ≪ F. A lemma (if F'_G ≪ G and H ≤ G, then H ∥ F'_G implies H ∥ F') gives z ∥ F', and one takes G = z.

Purpose. This is preparatory: it lays down the regularity and subdivision properties needed before defining subdivisions of figures within the atlas axiomatics.
errors: No mathematical error is visible, but the argument is incomplete on this page. The key step is producing a piece z in the interior of X disjoint from F'_X. That step is only reduced, on p. 82, to a lemma whose proof breaks off.
The phrase 'en prenant n'importe quel x dans Omb(G) ... x dans Omb(G)' is redundant or garbled as transcribed. Most likely the intended restriction is to an x in the interior part of the shadow.
The deduction 'y ∥ F'' needs y to be a sub-piece of G (y ≤ G) and dissociation to be stable under passing to sub-pieces. This is implicit, not stated.

ideas.what: Point-free axiomatic 'atlas of figures' with shadows, interior relation ≪ and dissociation ∥, as a foundation for tame topology
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology / o-minimal-like structures; lattice-theoretic (point-free) topology
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight (1980s); point-free topology: Ehresmann, Isbell, Johnstone
ideas.where_published: Program only, not the axiomatics: called for in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5 'topologie modérée'

ideas.what: Proposition: if F' ≪ F and some non-empty G is dissociated from F' but meets F, then such a G exists with G ≪ F
ideas.modern_name: Regularity of closed tame sets (a closed set is the closure of its interior; F minus F' meets int F)

ideas.what: Reduction of the proposition to a localisation lemma: dissociation from F' can be tested on the restriction F'_G inside a piece G

missed.claim: Grothendieck begins the theory of subdivisions inside his axiomatic atlas of figures. He first wanted this regularity property as an axiom and then downgraded it to a proposition to be derived from At 9 and related axioms. The derivation is left incomplete here.
missed.quote: J'en viens aux subdivisions, dont il n'avait pas encore été question jusqu'à présent ! J'ai envie de poser [Axiome] Proposition
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It is a minor document of Grothendieck's own attempt at an axiomatic tame topology. The axiom/proposition hesitation may matter to anyone comparing his atlas axioms with o-minimal or point-free foundations. Mathematically, the content is elementary.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine regularity lemma within an unpublished axiomatic framework. The framework itself is of historical interest, but this page adds no notable new result.
transcription_corrections: The page opens 'J'en viens aux [axiomes] subdivisions, dont il n'avait pas encore été question jusqu'à présent ! J'ai envie de poser'. 'Axiomes' is crossed out and 'subdivisions' is underlined.
'Pour trouver une énoncé minimal' should read 'Pour trouver un énoncé minimal'.
'(pour Ax 9)' is probably '(par At 9)', consistent with the At-numbering on the previous page.
The inserted line reads 'x ∈ Om(F),' above 'tels que', followed by a crossed-out expression and then 'x ∦ y' (not-dissociated, with an overbar).
'et en outre puisque y ∥ F' !' reads in the image as 'et en outre y ∥ F'!', with 'puisque' as an interlinear insertion.
The final diagram is F' ≪ F, with ∨ (containment) below each; F'_X ≪ X; then ∨₀ below X; then x, with y beside it.
